key_insight: Increasing argon flow rate from 1600 to 1800 L/h during air plasma spraying of NiCrFeBSiC coatings produces thicker, denser coatings with better tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing plasma-spray gas flow is a practical lever for improving coating quality, wear resistance, and adhesion in thermal-spray surface engineering.
method: Air plasma sprayed self-fluxing NiCrFeBSiC metal-ceramic coatings on a substrate
Compared two argon flow rates: 1600 and 1800 L/h
Evaluated microstructure, microhardness, elastic modulus, friction, and scratch adhesion
evidence_signal: The abstract reports about a twofold increase in coating thickness and a twofold decrease in porosity at 1800 L/h, with friction coefficient dropping to about 0.107 and strong scratch-test adhesion.
watch_item: Results are based on only two argon flow settings, so the observed improvement may not capture the full process window or long-term service behavior.
paper_title: EFFECT OF ARGON FLOW RATE DURING AIR PLASMA SPRAYING ON THE STRUCTURE AND PROPERTIES OF NICRFEBSIC COATINGS
